actinium.options.title: Video Settings
actinium.options.description.idle: Point at a setting to see what it does and what it costs.
actinium.options.flag.requires_game_rest: Takes effect on the next launch.
actinium.options.renderDistance.tooltip: How far the world is drawn. The single largest cost in the frame: doubling it roughly quadruples the geometry the GPU has to consider.
actinium.options.simulationDistance.tool: How far entities and block updates keep running. Costs CPU, not GPU, so lowering it helps when the frame rate stutters rather than sags.
actinium.options.framerateLimit.tooltip: Caps how many frames are drawn per second. A cap below your display's refresh rate lowers power draw and fan noise at no visual cost.
actinium.options.vsync.tooltip: Locks presentation to the display refresh. On, Actinium uses the FIFO present mode and you get no tearing. Off, it prefers MAILBOX, which drops stale frames instead of tearing through them.
actinium.options.viewBobbing.tooltip: Sways the camera as you walk. Costs almost nothing to draw.
actinium.options.clouds.tooltip: Draws clouds above the world. Fancy clouds are volumetric and cost several hundred extra draws at long render distances.
actinium.options.mipmap.tooltip: Smooths distant textures. Higher levels remove the shimmer on faraway blocks and cost a small amount of VRAM.
actinium.options.entityShadows.tooltip: Draws a soft shadow under each entity. Cheap on its own, noticeable in a room full of mobs.
actinium.options.gpuCulling.tooltip: Culls hidden chunks on the GPU with a hierarchical depth buffer, then compacts the surviving draws into one indirect command. Removes most of the CPU cost of deciding what to draw. Turn it off if the world flickers on your driver.
Records chunk draw commands across worker threads into secondary command buffers. This is where most of Vulkan's advantage over OpenGL comes from.
actinium.options.chunkBuildThreads.toolt: Threads meshing chunk geometry. Auto leaves two cores free for the render and main threads. Raising it speeds up world loading and can starve the render thread.
actinium.options.persistentMapping.toolt: Keeps streaming buffers mapped so the CPU writes straight into memory the GPU reads. Turn it off only if a driver bug corrupts geometry.
actinium.options.interopMode.tooltip: How OpenGL calls from other mods are handled. Bridge runs them on a Vulkan-backed GL driver and supports everything. Translate converts them in Java, which is faster but only covers common calls. Off means OpenGL mods will not draw.
actinium.options.interopMode.unsupported: Your GPU driver does not expose external memory sharing, so Bridge mode is unavailable.
actinium.options.uniformRing.tooltip: Per-frame buffer holding shader uniform data. Raise it if the log reports a uniform ring overflow.
actinium.options.validationLayers.toolti: Checks every Vulkan call for misuse and logs what it finds. Costs roughly a third of your frame time. Turn this on when reporting a rendering bug.
actinium.options.shaderDebugInfo.tooltip: Compiles shaders unoptimised with source information, so RenderDoc captures show readable code.
actinium.config.title: Actinium
actinium.options.unavailable.backend: Actinium is not driving the renderer. VulkanMod owns the Vulkan backend in this setup, so this setting has no effect.
actinium.options.unavailable.rendererMod: Actinium's own renderer is running, so the built-in VulkanMod renderer this setting configures is off.
actinium.options.unavailable.vulkanmod: VulkanMod is not installed, so there is no Vulkan renderer to configure.
actinium.options.unavailable.setting: This build of VulkanMod has no setting called '%s'.
actinium.options.ao.tooltip: Darkens block corners where light is blocked. Sub-block mode shades within a block face as well, which looks better on stairs and slabs and costs a little more to mesh.
actinium.options.occlusionCulling.toolti: Tests chunks against a hierarchical depth pyramid on the GPU and skips the ones nothing can see. The largest win underground and in dense builds. Experimental in VulkanMod: turn it off if terrain flickers or disappears.
actinium.options.indirectDraw.tooltip: Issues terrain as one indirect draw over a GPU-built command buffer instead of one draw per chunk section. This is where most of Vulkan's CPU advantage over OpenGL comes from.
actinium.options.advCulling.tooltip: How aggressively chunks outside the view are discarded. Aggressive skips the most and can clip geometry at the screen edge when you turn quickly. Conservative keeps more and draws more.
actinium.options.entityCulling.tooltip: Skips entities that no visible block face can see. Pays for itself in mob farms and villages, does almost nothing in an empty world.
actinium.options.leavesCulling.tooltip: Skips the inside faces of leaf blocks that sit two or more leaves deep, where the leaves in front already hide them. Trees look the same from outside and draw far fewer triangles; in a dense forest this is the biggest GPU saving. Turn it off to see every inner leaf face.
actinium.options.backFaceCulling.tooltip: Drops triangles facing away from the camera during meshing. Turn it off only if a mod's blocks render inside out.
actinium.options.builderThreads.tooltip: Threads meshing chunk geometry. Auto leaves one core for the render thread. Raising it loads the world faster and can starve rendering while it does.
actinium.options.frameQueue.tooltip: How many frames the CPU may run ahead of the GPU. Higher smooths out frame time spikes and adds input latency. Rebuilds the swapchain when changed.
actinium.options.uniqueOpaqueLayer.toolt: Merges solid and cutout terrain into one render pass. Fewer pipeline switches per frame. Turn it off if blocks with cutout textures render wrongly.
actinium.options.interopEnabled.tooltip: Intercept OpenGL calls other mods make directly to LWJGL. This does not render anything yet: buffers and textures reach the GPU, but no draw call has ever gone through the layer. Leave it off unless you are developing Actinium.
actinium.options.fpsCounter.tooltip: Shows your frame rate on screen while you play. Simple shows the average; Detailed adds the lowest and highest frame rate of the last half second. Updates twice a second and hides with F1 or the F3 screen.
actinium.options.fpsCounterPosition.tool: Which corner of the screen the FPS counter sits in.
actinium.options.unavailable.fpsCounterO: Turn the FPS Counter on to choose where it sits.
actinium.options.unavailable.fullscreenO: Only used in exclusive fullscreen. Set Window Mode to Fullscreen to change it.
actinium.options.windowMode.tooltip: Windowed, a borderless window covering the screen, or exclusive fullscreen. Exclusive fullscreen uses the resolution and refresh rate below and can give the lowest latency.
actinium.options.resolution.tooltip: The display mode used in exclusive fullscreen.
actinium.options.refreshRate.tooltip: The refresh rate used in exclusive fullscreen. The choices depend on the resolution.
actinium.options.guiScale.tooltip: Size of menus, the hotbar and text. Auto picks the largest scale that fits the window.
actinium.options.gamma.tooltip: How bright dark areas appear. Costs nothing.
actinium.options.menuBlur.tooltip: Blurs the world behind menus. Higher values cost a little GPU time while a menu is open.
actinium.options.attackIndicator.tooltip: Shows the attack cooldown under the crosshair or beside the hotbar.
actinium.options.autosaveIndicator.toolt: Shows an icon in the corner while the world saves.
Which chunk rebuilds happen immediately on the main thread. Nearby or player-affected rebuilds remove visible pop-in around you and can cost frame time while building.
actinium.options.graphics.tooltip: Fast draws opaque leaves and simpler weather. Fancy draws transparent leaves and fuller effects. Fabulous is not available with the Vulkan renderer.
actinium.options.particles.tooltip: How many particles are spawned. Decreased and Minimal help in heavy redstone or combat.
actinium.options.biomeBlend.tooltip: Blends grass, foliage and water colour across biome borders. Wider blends make chunk rebuilds slower.
actinium.options.entityDistance.tooltip: How far away entities are drawn, relative to the default. Lower it for crowded farms.
actinium.options.animateOnlyVisibleTextu: Only updates animated textures that were on screen in the last frame. Saves the upload for water, lava, fire and modded animations you can't see. Turn off if an animation on some modded block looks frozen.
actinium.options.textureAnimations.toolt: Animates water, lava, fire and other animated textures. Off saves the upload each animated frame costs.
actinium.options.deviceSelector.tooltip: The GPU the renderer uses. Auto prefers a discrete card.
The GPU the renderer uses. Auto prefers a discrete card. In use now: %s
actinium.options.glContextBridge.tooltip: Gives mods that call OpenGL directly a real, hidden OpenGL context. Mods built on Veil need it to start. Anything they draw through OpenGL is not shown on screen.
actinium.options.weatherQuality.tooltip: How rain and snow are drawn. Fast draws them in a smaller area around you with fewer splash particles. Default follows the Graphics setting.
actinium.options.leavesQuality.tooltip: Fancy leaves show the sky and blocks through their gaps. Fast leaves are solid and cheaper to draw in dense forests. Default follows the Graphics setting.
actinium.options.vignette.tooltip: Darkens the edges of the screen slightly, as in vanilla.
